title: Converting Between Single-Instance and Recurring Components via Edit (None <-> RRULE)

citations.verbatim_quote: The entire event can be rescheduled using a "REQUEST".  This is done by using the "UID" of the event to reschedule and including the modified "RRULE".  Note that since this is an entire rescheduling of the event, any instance-specific information will be lost, unless explicitly included with the update "REQUEST".

Description:  The recurrence rule, if specified, is used in computing the recurrence set.  The recurrence set is the complete set of recurrence instances for a calendar component.  The recurrence set is generated by considering the initial "DTSTART" property along with the "RRULE", "RDATE", and "EXDATE" properties contained within the recurring component.  The "DTSTART" property defines the first instance in the recurrence set.

If present, this JSCalendar object represents one occurrence of a recurring JSCalendar object.  If present, the "recurrenceRules" and "recurrenceOverrides" properties MUST NOT be present.

   The value is a date-time either produced by the "recurrenceRules" of the base event or added as a key to the "recurrenceOverrides" property of the base event.

rationale: Per RFC 5545 Section 3.8.5.3 and RFC 5546 Section 4.4.7, a calendar component referenced by its `UID` (with `recurrence_id=None`) may have an `RRULE` added, modified, or removed. Two boundary transitions arise when editing a component with `recurrence_id=None`: (1) Converting a non-recurring component (`rrule=None, rdate=[]`) to a recurring series (`rrule='FREQ=...'`): the component is updated in place with the new `RRULE` (retaining its `UID` and `CREATED` timestamp, incrementing `SEQUENCE`, and updating `DTSTAMP`/`LAST-MODIFIED`), and subsequent timeline expansions generate the full recurrence set starting at `DTSTART`. (2) Converting a recurring series (`rrule='FREQ=...'`) to a single-instance component (`rrule=None, rdate=[]`): because the component is no longer recurring, any previously recorded `EXDATE` entries on the component and any sibling `RECURRENCE-ID` override components (per RFC 8984 Section 4.3.1, which exist only as occurrences of a recurring base object) become invalid and must be cleared/removed so only the single non-recurring component remains in the calendar.
store_implication: When editing a component by `UID` with `recurrence_id=None`: (1) `None -> RRULE`: if the existing component had `rrule=None` and the edit supplies a non-null `rrule`, the store MUST permit setting `rrule` on the component in place and expand all occurrences generated by the new `rrule` on the timeline; (2) `RRULE -> None`: if the existing component was recurring and the edit clears `rrule` to `None` (with empty `rdate`), the store MUST update the master component in place with `rrule=None`, clear `exdate=[]`, and remove all standalone override components (`uid == target_uid`, `recurrence_id is not None`, and neither `rrule` nor `rdate` is present) from the calendar.
edge_cases_and_counterexamples: Adding an `RRULE` (`FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=3`) to a previously non-recurring event via `edit(uid, recurrence_id=None, patch={'rrule': 'FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=3'})`: must succeed (must NOT be rejected by the single-instance override guard, which only forbids changing `rrule` when `recurrence_id is not None` and `range == NONE`) and must expand to 3 occurrences on the timeline.

Removing `RRULE` (`patch={'rrule': None}`) from a recurring series that had an `EXDATE` on May 2 and a `RECURRENCE-ID` override component on May 3: the master component becomes a single non-recurring event on May 1 with `exdate=[]`, and the May 3 override component MUST be removed so it does not linger on the timeline as an orphan.

Preserving `RELATED-TO` children: converting a parent component between non-recurring and recurring in place (`recurrence_id=None`) must NOT trigger cascading deletion of `RELATED-TO;RELTYPE=PARENT` child components.

scenarios.name: convert_single_event_to_recurring_series_in_place
scenarios.description: Editing a non-recurring event with recurrence_id=None to add RRULE=FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=3 converts the event in place into a 3-day recurring series.

scenarios.name: convert_recurring_series_to_single_event_clears_exdate_and_overrides
scenarios.description: Editing a recurring series (that has an EXDATE on May 2 and a RECURRENCE-ID override on May 3) with recurrence_id=None and rrule=None converts the master component into a single-instance event, clears exdate, and removes the orphaned May 3 override component.
